metadata.summary: Sky Sports Cricket's Stuart Broad is excited at what new England Test coach Stephen Fleming can bring to Joe Root's captaincy as the New Zealander prepares for his first assignment in the role in South Africa this winter.
metadata.content: Stephen Fleming: Stuart Broad excited at what new England Test cricket coach can do for Joe Root's captaincy | Cricket News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Opinion Stephen Fleming: Stuart Broad excited at what new England Test cricket coach can do for Joe Root's captaincy Sky Sports pundit Stuart Broad on Stephen Fleming-Joe Root relationship: "Where Joe needs a bit of help with his captaincy is taking a bit of weight off his shoulders at times, allowing him to concentrate on batting, make tactical decisions and get feedback throughout to help England out" Stuart Broad Cricket expert Saturday 19 September 2026 20:03, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player New England Test coach Stephen Fleming says he was involved in the appointment of Joe Root as captain and explains why he expects him to be a success Sky Sports Cricket's Stuart Broad is excited at what new England Test coach Stephen Fleming can bring to Joe Root's captaincy as the New Zealander prepares for his first assignment in the role in South Africa this winter. Fleming was named as countryman Brendon McCullum's successor in late July but did not lead the side for the recent 3-0 sweep of Pakistan due to family commitments. The 53-year-old recently flew to England for a short trip to chat with ECB officials and Test skipper Root as well as the counties, and was with the national team as they completed a 3-0 T20I whitewash under white-ball coach McCullum in Manchester on Saturday . messages.text: Littler threatens Dutch boycott after boos and whistles in Amsterdam

metadata.summary: Luke Littler threatened to boycott tournaments in the Netherlands after being booed and whistled at during his win over Nathan Aspinall at the World Series of Darts.
metadata.content: World Series of Darts Finals: Luke Littler threatens Netherlands tournament boycott after being booed and whistled at by Amsterdam crowd | Darts News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Update World Series of Darts Finals: Luke Littler threatens Netherlands tournament boycott after being booed and whistled at by Amsterdam crowd Luke 'The Nuke' Littler was booed and whistled at by fans in the Netherlands during his dramatic second-round victory over Nathan Aspinall; the world No 1 threatened a boycott of Dutch darts events, similar to what he has done in Germany as a result of his treatment from fans there By David Rivers Sunday 20 September 2026 09:06, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Luke Littler and Nathan Aspinall battle it out until the very end where Littler delivered a 12-darter to squeeze into the last eight at the World Series of Darts Finals Luke Littler threatened to boycott tournaments in the Netherlands after being booed and whistled at during his win over Nathan Aspinall at the World Series of Darts. 'The Nuke' moved a step closer to becoming the first man to win all 10 major televised tournaments in a calendar year, having triumphed in the first five, with a hard-fought win over Aspinall in Amsterdam. Littler won the last two legs to prevail 10-9 but the match was overshadowed by the crowd's behaviour towards him.
